summary:
Team Name: Junior Mars Launch
About Our Team:
Junior Mars Launch is led by an 11-year-old student whose passion for planets and dream of one day traveling to Mars inspired this entire project. Created, designed, and programmed by him—with his mother joining solely as a supportive partner to help bring his vision to life—the team reflects a young explorer's determination to start planning for Mars today by helping other kids understand how rockets really work.
details: Our Objectives: Reduce Trial-and-Error Through Pre-Flight Planning: Empower children and youth (ages 8+) to think like real NASA engineers before launching—using his custom Scratch calculator to validate liftoff Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR 1.2–1.53), Delta-v (Δv), and mission Budget prior to building rockets in free mobile simulators like Roblox's "Make a Rocket" (referenced strictly for educational purposes). Promote STEM Inclusion Across the Portuguese-Speaking World (>260 Million Speakers): Break down language and hardware barriers by building the tool in Portuguese—a language spoken by more than 260 million people across Portugal, Brazil, Timor-Leste, and the PALOP (Portuguese-speaking African countries)—while introducing key English aerospace terms (TWR, Δv, Budget). Inspired by free, smartphone-accessible platforms, it enables millions of Portuguese-speaking children and youth to learn real space science using just a mobile phone. Turn a Childhood Dream into Action: Show other kids that you don't have to wait until you grow up to explore space engineering—starting right now with curiosity, basic math, and a love for Mars.
